title: 2 Corinthians Chapter 11 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 2 Corinthians chapter 11 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 2 Corinthians Chapter 11 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 2 Corinthians Chapter 11.

questions.question: In 2 Corinthians 11, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
questions.explanation: The first mention in the chapter is Paul's request to bear with him in his folly, found in 2 Corinthians 11:1.

questions.question: What does Paul express he has espoused the Corinthians to?
questions.explanation: Paul mentions he has espoused them to one husband to present them as a chaste virgin to Christ, as stated in 2 Corinthians 11:2.

questions.question: What does Paul fear regarding the Corinthians?
questions.explanation: Paul fears that their minds should be corrupted from the simplicity that is in Christ, as mentioned in 2 Corinthians 11:3.

questions.question: What does Paul say about someone who preaches another Jesus?
options: You might well bear with him
questions.correctAnswer: You might well bear with him
questions.explanation: Paul states that if someone preaches another Jesus, you might well bear with him, as per 2 Corinthians 11:4.

questions.question: How does Paul compare himself to the chiefest apostles?
questions.explanation: Paul states he was not a whit behind the very chiefest apostles, according to 2 Corinthians 11:5.

questions.question: What does Paul say about his speech and knowledge?
questions.explanation: Paul admits to being rude in speech yet not in knowledge, as stated in 2 Corinthians 11:6.

questions.question: Why does Paul ask if he committed an offense?
questions.explanation: Paul questions if he committed an offense in abasing himself that they might be exalted because he preached the gospel freely, as per 2 Corinthians 11:7.

questions.question: What did Paul do to serve the Corinthians?
questions.explanation: Paul states he robbed other churches, taking wages of them to do the Corinthians service, as found in 2 Corinthians 11:8.

questions.question: Who supplied what was lacking to Paul?
questions.explanation: Paul mentions that the brethren which came from Macedonia supplied what was lacking to him, as stated in 2 Corinthians 11:9.

questions.question: What does Paul claim about his boasting in Achaia?
options: He has no reason to boast
questions.explanation: Paul declares that as the truth of Christ is in him, no man shall stop him of this boasting in the regions of Achaia, according to 2 Corinthians 11:10.

questions.question: What does Paul affirm about his love for the Corinthians?
questions.explanation: Paul asserts that he loves them and states that God knows this, as mentioned in 2 Corinthians 11:11.

questions.question: Paul was chargeable to no man when he was present with the Corinthians.
questions.explanation: Paul states in 2 Corinthians 11:9 that he was chargeable to no man when he was present with them.

questions.question: Paul preached the gospel of God freely to the Corinthians.
questions.explanation: Paul mentions in 2 Corinthians 11:7 that he preached the gospel of God freely.

questions.question: Paul was jealous over the Corinthians with worldly jealousy.
questions.explanation: Paul states he is jealous over them with godly jealousy in 2 Corinthians 11:2, not worldly jealousy.

questions.question: The Corinthians were warned about the subtleness of the serpent in relation to their faith.
questions.explanation: While Paul mentions the serpent beguiling Eve in 2 Corinthians 11:3, he does not specifically warn the Corinthians about their faith in relation to this.

medium.title: 2 Corinthians Chapter 11 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 2 Corinthians Chapter 11 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to 2 Corinthians 11:13, how are false apostles described?
options: Deceitful workers, transforming themselves into the apostles of Christ
Truthful servants, preaching the gospel faithfully
Zealous believers, shining as lights in the darkness
questions.correctAnswer: Deceitful workers, transforming themselves into the apostles of Christ
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 11:13 states that false apostles are 'deceitful workers, transforming themselves into the apostles of Christ.'

questions.question: What does 2 Corinthians 11:15 say will happen to the end of Satan's ministers if they transform themselves as ministers of righteousness, as commanded in 2 Corinthians 11:14?
options: Their end shall be according to their works
They will be exalted among believers
They will receive blessings from God
questions.correctAnswer: Their end shall be according to their works
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 11:15 explains that the ministers of Satan, though transformed as ministers of righteousness as described in 2 Corinthians 11:14, will have their end according to their works.

questions.question: Why does Paul say he will boast a little according to 2 Corinthians 11:16?
options: To prevent others from thinking him a fool
To show his superiority over others
To boast of his wealth and achievements
To gain followers among the Corinthians
questions.correctAnswer: To prevent others from thinking him a fool
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 11:16 shows Paul saying 'Let no man think me a fool; if otherwise, yet as a fool receive me, that I may boast myself a little,' indicating he boasts to avoid being seen as a fool.

questions.question: How does Paul explain his confidence in boasting in 2 Corinthians 11:17 and how is it connected to his statement in 2 Corinthians 11:16?
options: He speaks foolishly but with confidence, following his request not to be thought a fool
He speaks boldly as commanded by the Lord
He refuses to boast at all
He boasts only when others do
questions.correctAnswer: He speaks foolishly but with confidence, following his request not to be thought a fool
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 11:17 continues Paul’s explanation from verse 16, stating he speaks not after the Lord but 'as it were foolishly, in this confidence of boasting,' showing his self-aware confidence.

questions.question: What practical lesson about discernment can be learned from Paul’s description of Satan in 2 Corinthians 11:14?
options: Appearances can be deceptive, so believers must carefully discern true from false teachers
Satan openly reveals his intentions to deceive
All who claim to be ministers of righteousness are trustworthy
Believers should not question spiritual leaders
questions.correctAnswer: Appearances can be deceptive, so believers must carefully discern true from false teachers
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 11:14 warns that Satan is transformed into an angel of light, teaching the need for discernment because evil can appear good.

questions.question: According to 2 Corinthians 11:20, what kinds of abuses were the Corinthians suffering from false teachers?
options: Being brought into bondage, devoured, taken from, exalted over, and smitten on the face
questions.correctAnswer: Being brought into bondage, devoured, taken from, exalted over, and smitten on the face
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 11:20 lists multiple abuses the Corinthians endured from false teachers, including bondage, being devoured, taken from, exalted, and smitten.

questions.question: Why does Paul say he will also be bold in 2 Corinthians 11:21?
options: Because some are bold, he will be bold as well, even if foolishly
Because he fears the false teachers
Because he wants to avoid suffering
Because he is commanded by the Lord
questions.correctAnswer: Because some are bold, he will be bold as well, even if foolishly
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 11:21 says Paul speaks about boldness, stating 'Howbeit whereinsoever any is bold, (I speak foolishly,) I am bold also,' showing his resolve to match others’ boldness.

questions.question: What identity claims does Paul make in 2 Corinthians 11:22 to establish his authority?
options: He claims to be a Hebrew, an Israelite, and seed of Abraham
He claims to be a Roman citizen
He claims to have been a Pharisee
He claims to be a disciple of Peter
questions.correctAnswer: He claims to be a Hebrew, an Israelite, and seed of Abraham
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 11:22 shows Paul asserting his identity as Hebrew, Israelite, and seed of Abraham to align himself with true spiritual heritage.

questions.question: How does Paul describe his preaching of the gospel in 2 Corinthians 11:7 and what principle can be applied from this?
options: He preached freely without seeking personal gain, teaching the value of selfless service
He charged high fees for his preaching
He sought personal glory in his message
He preached only to wealthy people
questions.correctAnswer: He preached freely without seeking personal gain, teaching the value of selfless service
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 11:7 shows Paul preaching the gospel freely, emphasizing selflessness and service without personal profit.

questions.question: What does 2 Corinthians 11:9 teach about Paul’s attitude towards receiving help and being a burden?
options: He avoids being burdensome so others are not charged, showing humility and responsibility
He demands support from the Corinthians
He refuses any help from others
He relies only on his own resources
questions.correctAnswer: He avoids being burdensome so others are not charged, showing humility and responsibility
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 11:9 explains Paul kept himself from being burdensome, highlighting humility and responsibility in ministry.

questions.question: What reason does Paul give in 2 Corinthians 11:11 for his boldness and boasting?
options: Because he wants to shame others
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 11:11 answers 'Wherefore? because I love you not? God knoweth,' showing love as the root of his boldness.

questions.question: According to 2 Corinthians 11:1-2, what is Paul’s relationship to the Corinthians compared to a husband and a virgin?
options: He has espoused them to one husband, Christ, to present them as a chaste virgin
He sees them as strangers with no commitment
He views them as enemies in conflict
He regards them as spiritual children needing discipline
questions.correctAnswer: He has espoused them to one husband, Christ, to present them as a chaste virgin
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 11:2 describes Paul’s godly jealousy, espousing the Corinthians to Christ as a chaste virgin.

questions.question: True or False: According to 2 Corinthians 11:4, Paul warns the Corinthians against receiving another spirit or gospel different from the one they accepted.
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 11:4 warns the Corinthians about receiving another Jesus, spirit, or gospel different from what Paul preached.

questions.question: True or False: In 2 Corinthians 11:6, Paul admits he is rude in speech and lacking in knowledge.
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 11:6 states Paul is rude in speech but not in knowledge, showing his competence despite rough speech.

questions.question: True or False: 2 Corinthians 11:18 says Paul will not glory after the flesh like many others.
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 11:18 says 'Seeing that many glory after the flesh, I will glory also,' showing Paul does glory after the flesh as well.

hard.title: 2 Corinthians Chapter 11 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 2 Corinthians Chapter 11.

questions.question: According to 2 Corinthians 11:23, Paul claims to be more abundant than the ministers of Christ in what?
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 11:23 states Paul is more abundant in labours, stripes, prisons, and deaths than the ministers of Christ.

questions.question: How many times did Paul receive forty stripes save one from the Jews as per 2 Corinthians 11:24?
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 11:24 clearly states Paul received forty stripes save one five times from the Jews.

questions.question: Which of the following sufferings is NOT mentioned by Paul in 2 Corinthians 11:25?
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 11:25 mentions being beaten with rods thrice, stoned once, shipwrecked thrice, but does not mention four imprisonments (imprisonments are mentioned elsewhere).

questions.question: In 2 Corinthians 11:26, Paul lists various perils he faced. Which peril is NOT included in this list?
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 11:26 lists many perils including false brethren, city, robbers, but does not mention perils by angels.

questions.question: According to 2 Corinthians 11:28, what additional burden comes upon Paul daily besides external hardships?
options: The care of all the churches
questions.correctAnswer: The care of all the churches
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 11:28 states that beside outward sufferings, Paul has the daily burden of caring for all the churches.

questions.question: How did Paul escape from Damascus as described in 2 Corinthians 11:33?
options: He was let down through a window in a basket
He fled at night through the city gates
He disguised himself and escaped on foot
He was released by the governor
questions.correctAnswer: He was let down through a window in a basket
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 11:33 describes Paul being let down in a basket through a window in the city wall to escape.

questions.question: What does the Greek word 'ἐνδεής' (endeēs) in 2 Corinthians 11:27 mean?
questions.explanation: In 2 Corinthians 11:27, the Greek word 'ἐνδεής' means lacking or needy, describing Paul's state of cold and nakedness.

questions.question: Which literary device is primarily used in 2 Corinthians 11:23-27 as Paul lists his sufferings?
questions.explanation: The passage 2 Corinthians 11:23-27 uses parallelism by listing a series of related sufferings in a structured, repetitive pattern.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage connects to Paul's description of being beaten with 'forty stripes save one' in 2 Corinthians 11:24?
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 25:3 sets the limit of forty stripes save one as a lawful punishment, which Paul references in 2 Corinthians 11:24.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes Paul's experience of being let down in a basket in 2 Corinthians 11:33?
questions.explanation: Acts 9:23-25 recounts Paul's escape from Damascus by being let down in a basket, paralleling 2 Corinthians 11:33.

questions.question: What comes immediately before Paul's statement 'If I must needs glory, I will glory of the things which concern mine infirmities' in 2 Corinthians 11?
options: Paul asks who is weak and if he is not weak
Paul boasts about his visions and revelations
questions.correctAnswer: Paul asks who is weak and if he is not weak
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 11:29 precedes verse 30 with Paul asking 'Who is weak, and I am not weak?', leading into his boasting about infirmities in 11:30.

questions.question: Which type of literary device is illustrated by Paul’s contrasting 'false apostles' and himself as 'apostles of Christ' in 2 Corinthians 11:13-15?
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 11:13-15 employs antithesis by contrasting false apostles with true apostles of Christ.

questions.question: In the context of 2 Corinthians 11:2-3, Paul's reference to the serpent beguiling Eve serves as a typology for what?
options: The corruption of the Corinthians' minds from Christ’s simplicity
The story of salvation through Christ
The establishment of the new covenant
The fulfillment of Old Testament prophecy
questions.correctAnswer: The corruption of the Corinthians' minds from Christ’s simplicity
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 11:3 uses the serpent's deception of Eve as a typology for how the Corinthians’ minds might be corrupted from the simplicity in Christ.

questions.question: Paul’s boasting in 2 Corinthians 11:18-21 about 'glorying after the flesh' can be understood as using which rhetorical strategy?
questions.explanation: In 2 Corinthians 11:18-21, Paul ironically boasts 'after the flesh' to expose and critique false teachers who glory in worldly status.

questions.question: Paul claims in 2 Corinthians 11:31 that 'The God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ... knoweth that I lie not.' This assertion in Greek is an example of which literary device?
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 11:31 is an oath or solemn affirmation invoking God as witness to the truthfulness of Paul's statement.

theological.title: 2 Corinthians Chapter 11 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 2 Corinthians Chapter 11 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does 2 Corinthians 11:2 teach about the nature of salvation?
options: Salvation involves a betrothal to Christ, emphasizing purity and covenant faithfulness
Salvation is primarily a legal declaration without relational commitment
Salvation depends on human wisdom and eloquence
Salvation is achieved through adherence to Mosaic Law
questions.correctAnswer: Salvation involves a betrothal to Christ, emphasizing purity and covenant faithfulness
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 11:2 speaks of Paul espousing the Corinthians to one husband, Christ, to present them as a chaste virgin, indicating the covenantal and relational nature of salvation.

questions.question: What doctrine about human sin does 2 Corinthians 11:3 teach?
options: Human minds can be corrupted from the simplicity found in Christ, paralleling the deception of Eve
Human sin is only external and does not affect the mind
Sin is irrelevant once one becomes a Christian
Human nature is inherently good and cannot be corrupted
questions.correctAnswer: Human minds can be corrupted from the simplicity found in Christ, paralleling the deception of Eve
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 11:3 compares the potential corruption of the Corinthians’ minds to Eve's deception by the serpent, showing the ongoing vulnerability to sin’s subtlety.

questions.question: What doctrine about false teaching does 2 Corinthians 11:4 teach?
options: False teachers promote another Jesus, a different spirit, or another gospel, which believers must discern
Any teaching that differs from Paul’s is automatically heresy
There is only one gospel, but many legitimate spirits
Differences in gospel presentations are acceptable as long as they encourage faith
questions.correctAnswer: False teachers promote another Jesus, a different spirit, or another gospel, which believers must discern
questions.explanation: Verse 4 warns against accepting another Jesus, spirit, or gospel, highlighting the necessity of doctrinal purity and vigilance against false teaching.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does 2 Corinthians 11:31 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 11:31 states that God knows the truth of Paul’s words, illustrating God's attribute of omniscience—His all-knowing nature.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does 2 Corinthians 11:11 illustrate?
questions.explanation: Paul’s rhetorical question in 11:11, 'because I love you not?' reveals God's love as the motivating force behind Paul's actions toward the Corinthians.

questions.question: How does 2 Corinthians 11:13–15 connect to broader biblical themes about spiritual deception?
options: It reflects the biblical theme of Satan masquerading as an angel of light to deceive believers
It teaches that all angels are deceptive and untrustworthy
It denies the reality of spiritual warfare
It asserts that deception only comes from human sources
questions.correctAnswer: It reflects the biblical theme of Satan masquerading as an angel of light to deceive believers
questions.explanation: Verses 13-15 describe false apostles as deceitful workers and relate their deception to Satan’s disguise as an angel of light, echoing biblical teaching on spiritual deception and warfare.

questions.question: How does the description of Paul's sufferings in 2 Corinthians 11:23-27 prepare readers for understanding the cost of apostleship in the New Testament?
options: It highlights the severe trials and sacrifices involved in apostolic ministry, emphasizing perseverance
It suggests apostleship is free from hardship
It indicates that physical suffering is irrelevant to spiritual authority
It claims apostles should avoid persecution at all costs
questions.correctAnswer: It highlights the severe trials and sacrifices involved in apostolic ministry, emphasizing perseverance
questions.explanation: Paul’s recounting of his many hardships underscores the high cost and perseverance required in apostolic ministry, a key theme in New Testament witness.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses 2 Corinthians 11:7 and 11:8 teach about Christian ministry and self-support?
options: Christian ministry should be freely given without seeking financial gain, even at personal cost
Ministers should prioritize personal wealth accumulation
Christian ministry is incompatible with any form of financial hardship
Ministers must always accept payment from those they serve
questions.correctAnswer: Christian ministry should be freely given without seeking financial gain, even at personal cost
questions.explanation: In 11:7 and 11:8, Paul highlights that he preached the gospel freely and even ‘robbed’ other churches of their support to serve the Corinthians, emphasizing voluntary self-support in ministry.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses 2 Corinthians 11:29 and 11:30 teach about Christian weakness and boasting?
options: Christian boasting should focus on weaknesses, which reveal reliance on God rather than self
Boasting in strength is the mark of true spirituality
Weakness is a sign of failure and should be hidden
Boasting is always inappropriate in Christian life
questions.correctAnswer: Christian boasting should focus on weaknesses, which reveal reliance on God rather than self
questions.explanation: Verses 29-30 show Paul’s willingness to boast about his infirmities, reflecting a theology that values weakness as revealing dependence on God.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do 2 Corinthians 11:1 and 11:16 teach about apostolic humility and boasting?
options: Paul uses a paradoxical approach, embracing a 'foolish' boasting to defend his ministry while exhibiting humility
Paul rejects all forms of boasting as sinful
Paul claims to be the wisest apostle without humility
Boasting is used to elevate oneself above others
questions.correctAnswer: Paul uses a paradoxical approach, embracing a 'foolish' boasting to defend his ministry while exhibiting humility
questions.explanation: In 11:1 and 11:16, Paul invites readers to bear with his 'folly' and accept his 'foolish' boasting, reflecting a nuanced rhetorical strategy blending humility and defense of ministry.

questions.question: Sceptics claim Paul’s boasting in 2 Corinthians 11:22-29 shows arrogance and contradicts Christian humility. What does 2 Corinthians 11:22-29 actually teach?
options: Paul’s boasting highlights the severe sufferings he endured as evidence of authentic apostleship and humility through weakness
Paul boasts to exalt himself above other apostles
Paul’s boasting is a sign he rejected humility
Paul claims to be sinless and perfect
questions.correctAnswer: Paul’s boasting highlights the severe sufferings he endured as evidence of authentic apostleship and humility through weakness
questions.explanation: Verses 22-29 detail Paul’s sufferings, which serve as marks of genuine apostleship and humility, countering claims of arrogance.

questions.question: What doctrine does 2 Corinthians 11:10 teach about the truthfulness of Christ in Paul’s ministry?
options: The truth of Christ in Paul’s life empowers him to boldly boast in ministry despite opposition
Boasting is forbidden regardless of truth
Truth is irrelevant to ministry confidence
Paul’s boasting is based on worldly success
questions.correctAnswer: The truth of Christ in Paul’s life empowers him to boldly boast in ministry despite opposition
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 11:10 shows Paul declaring that the truth of Christ within him prevents anyone from stopping his boasting, highlighting divine empowerment in ministry.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is especially demonstrated by God’s knowledge of Paul’s honesty in 2 Corinthians 11:31?
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 11:31 states God 'knoweth that I lie not,' emphasizing God’s all-knowing nature.

questions.question: How does 2 Corinthians 11:9 doctrinally contribute to the understanding of Christian community and support?
options: It teaches the principle of mutual aid within the body of Christ to prevent burdensomeness
It promotes individualism without church support
It encourages reliance solely on personal wealth
It forbids receiving help from others
questions.correctAnswer: It teaches the principle of mutual aid within the body of Christ to prevent burdensomeness
questions.explanation: Verse 9 shows Paul receiving provision from brethren from Macedonia to avoid being a burden to the Corinthians, illustrating mutual care in Christian fellowship.

questions.question: What theological theme is prepared for by Paul’s description of false apostles in 2 Corinthians 11:13, as it relates to the wider New Testament?
options: The ongoing challenge of distinguishing true from false teachers in the church
The acceptance of all teachings as equally valid
The idea that apostolic authority is irrelevant
The rejection of any form of church discipline
questions.correctAnswer: The ongoing challenge of distinguishing true from false teachers in the church
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 11:13 warns of false apostles, preparing readers for broader New Testament concerns about doctrinal purity and church discernment.
